summary: Microsoft has launched a new product family called Microsoft Entra, which consolidates all of its identity and access capabilities. This includes Azure Active Directory, a new Cloud Infrastructure Entitlement Management (CIEM) solution called Microsoft Entra Permissions Management, and a decentralized identity offering, Microsoft Entra Verified ID. The initiative aims to provide a unified trust fabric for the digital ecosystem, securing access across various cloud environments and enabling privacy-respecting digital interactions.

title: Accenture, Microsoft and Avanade expand partnership to help organizations tackle their greatest sustainability challenges
summary: Accenture, Microsoft, and Avanade have expanded their partnership to help organizations address sustainability challenges, with an initial focus on achieving net zero and future plans for broader ESG issues. They will invest in co-developing carbon-efficient solutions and offer advisory services for reducing emissions, transitioning to new energy sources, and minimizing waste. The collaboration will target digital manufacturing transitions, low carbon energy transitions, sustainable IT with Microsoft Azure, and ESG measurement and analytics using the Microsoft Cloud for Sustainability.

title: ASGN Acquires ServiceNow IT Consulting Partner GlideFast for $350M -
summary: ASGN is acquiring GlideFast Consulting, a ServiceNow IT consulting partner, for $350 million in cash from private equity firm BV Investment Partners. The deal is expected to close in July 2022 and aligns with ASGN's strategic growth plan to reach $6 billion in revenues by 2024. GlideFast, founded in 2015, expects to generate $95 million in revenue for 2022 with mid-teen EBITDA margins.

title: A digital conflict between Russia and Ukraine rages on behind the scenes of war
summary: A behind-the-scenes digital conflict is ongoing between Russia and Ukraine, with the U.S. also conducting offensive cyber operations. Microsoft's Head of Customer Security and Trust, Tom Burt, details how the company has observed destructive cyberattacks leading up to and during the invasion, noting similarities between Russian cyber and physical military objectives. This "hybrid war" poses a threat of collateral damage to Western companies, highlighting the critical role of private sector insights and collaboration with governments.

title: What Can a Multi-Factor Screening Methodology Do for Your Core Equity Exposure?
summary: This article discusses how applying a multi-factor screening methodology, focusing on value, quality, and momentum, can enhance core equity exposure for large-cap stock portfolios. It highlights research from FlexShares suggesting that this approach can deliver superior risk-adjusted returns compared to the broad large-cap market. The FlexShares US Quality Large Cap Index Fund (QLC) is presented as an example of an ETF that utilizes these factors.

title: Investing in Big Data with Data Center REITs
summary: This article explores the concept of investing in data center Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) as a way to gain exposure to the big data sector. While acknowledging the appeal of REITs for diversification and income, the authors argue that data center REITs carry significant risks, resembling tech stocks more than traditional real estate investments. They conclude that such REITs offer too much risk without sufficient upside potential, suggesting alternative investments like NVIDIA for data center growth exposure.

title: What Can a Multi-Factor Screening Methodology Do for Your Core Equity Exposure?
summary: This article discusses how applying a multi-factor screening methodology can improve risk-adjusted returns for large-cap equity portfolios. It highlights factors such as value, quality, and momentum, and introduces the FlexShares US Quality Large Cap Index Fund (QLC) which integrates these factors. The fund aims to provide benefits of these factor exposures while maintaining a similar risk profile to the broader large-cap market.

title: Teresa Carlson returns to Microsoft
summary: Teresa Carlson has rejoined Microsoft as a corporate Vice President and executive-in-residence, nearly 12 years after her previous departure. Carlson, a prominent figure in government cloud computing, left Amazon Web Services where she led their public sector growth, and then had a brief stint as chief growth officer at Splunk before her recent move back to Microsoft. Her return marks a significant development in her career trajectory within the technology industry.

title: MicroStrategy Incorporated Class A (MSTR)
summary: This page provides a detailed stock card for MicroStrategy Incorporated Class A (MSTR), showing its current share price, market capitalization, key financial ratios, and historical performance. It also includes peer comparisons, shareholding patterns, and an overview of the company's business as a bitcoin treasury and AI-powered enterprise analytics software provider. The article details FAQs related to the stock's price, ratios, 52-week range, and market cap.

title: Nvidia TAO Toolkit update aims to simplify deep learning model development
summary: Nvidia has updated its TAO Toolkit platform to simplify and accelerate deep learning model creation for enterprise applications, making AI development more accessible and less time-consuming. The toolkit now includes new capabilities like "bring your own model weights" and integration with TensorBoard for better visualization, along with the option to deploy as-a-service with REST APIs. While other companies have also worked on simplifying AI pipelines, analysts note that Nvidia's TAO Toolkit, with its low-code nature and pre-trained models, aims to speed up time-to-market for AI models and reduce the need for extensive data science expertise.

title: New report points to cyber risks in TVA control systems
summary: A recent oversight report revealed that the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) failed to properly implement cybersecurity standards for a control system managing flood and river systems in seven southeastern states. The report identified "inappropriate logical and physical access" and vulnerable operating systems at dams within the system. While the risk of a physical threat was considered low, the lack of clear ownership for the system's maintenance and operation heightened cybersecurity risks, prompting TVA to agree with the findings and commit to updates and clearer responsibilities.

title: Gen-trepreneur Z is making its mark on the future of small business
summary: A Microsoft Store report "Small Business State of Mind" highlights how Generation Z is redefining entrepreneurship. Gen Z small business owners prioritize social good, work unconventional hours, and are using platforms like TikTok for business advice, aiming for early retirement rather than traditional corporate paths. The article emphasizes their unique perspective on work, success, and the future of small business, despite challenges like inflation and data security risks.

title: 7 Blue-Chip Stocks to Buy for June 2022
summary: This article identifies seven blue-chip stocks for investors to consider buying in June 2022, emphasizing their stability and long-term potential amidst economic uncertainty. The list includes McDonald’s, Danaher, AT&T, Lockheed Martin, Microsoft, Chevron, and United Parcel Service, highlighting each company's resilience, strong fundamentals, and potential benefits like dividends or defensive qualities. The author suggests these large-cap companies offer a solid foundation for a portfolio, especially during turbulent economic times.

title: DocuSign and Microsoft Deepen Relationship to Accelerate Anywhere Work
summary: DocuSign and Microsoft have expanded their global strategic partnership to enhance how people collaborate and reach agreements digitally, particularly in the "anywhere economy." This collaboration involves new integrations and features across Microsoft 365, Dynamics 365, and Power Platform, aiming to streamline agreement processes, increase efficiency, and support remote work. Both companies will also deepen their use of each other's products to further automate internal workflows.

title: Why Has Microsoft Stock Been Falling; Will It Rebound? (NASDAQ:MSFT)
summary: Microsoft's stock has fallen 25% since its November peak, influenced by macroeconomic headwinds and a recent lowering of its fiscal fourth-quarter EPS and revenue guidance due to foreign exchange rates. Bears highlight these challenges, while bulls focus on the company's cloud business and other growth initiatives as potential rebound drivers. The article, written by Chuck Walston, explores these contrasting views on MSFT's future performance.

title: Intel Demonstrates Commitment to Security at RSA Conference 2022
summary: At RSA Conference 2022, Intel reinforced its commitment to security, showcasing innovations and partnerships aimed at addressing complex cyber challenges like hybrid workforces and connected devices. The company highlighted new solutions such as the Intel® NetSec Accelerator Reference Design, the expansion of Project Circuit Breaker, and advancements in hardware-based security with the Intel vPro® platform and confidential computing initiatives like Project Amber. Intel emphasized its holistic approach to security, spanning products, research, and ecosystem collaboration.

title: Oracle quietly closes $28B deal to buy electronic health records company Cerner
summary: Oracle has officially closed its $28 billion acquisition of electronic health records company Cerner, a deal initially announced just before Christmas last year. This move positions Oracle deeper into the healthcare market, aiming to bring Cerner's extensive workload to the Oracle cloud. Analyst Holger Mueller highlighted the strategic importance of this acquisition for Oracle's presence in a rapidly growing vertical industry.

title: Oracle closes $28B deal to buy EHR giant Cerner
summary: Oracle has finalized its $28.3 billion acquisition of health IT company Cerner, marking its largest acquisition to date and a significant move to expand into the healthcare market. The deal, which involved Oracle finalizing a stock tender offer with 69.2% of Cerner shares, aims to leverage Cerner as an "anchor asset" to scale Oracle's cloud business in hospitals and health systems. This acquisition positions Oracle to transform healthcare delivery through new information systems and addresses the growing trend of big tech companies investing heavily in the healthcare IT sector.

title: Weisong Shi recognized as leader in electric vehicle revolution
summary: Weisong Shi, a professor at Wayne State’s College of Engineering and leader of the Wayne Mobility Initiative, has been recognized by Crain’s Detroit Business as a notable leader in electric vehicles. His work in edge computing has influenced various industries, and he is the only academic on the prestigious list. Shi discusses the evolving mobility industry, the role of sensors, Wayne State's contributions to electric vehicle education, and how engineering training has adapted to new technologies.

title: InfoComm Panel: Enter The Metaverse, What Virtual Worlds Mean For AV
summary: An InfoComm panel discussed the metaverse's impact on audiovisual and design professionals, emphasizing its role as a new channel for marketing, training, entertainment, and work. Panelists urged businesses to strategically incorporate the metaverse, starting small and aligning initiatives with their brand values, while also addressing challenges like ethics and content protection. The discussion highlighted the potential for "digital twins" and immersive collaboration in the workplace, with Gartner predicting widespread adoption.

title: Microsoft announces four new employee workforce initiatives - Microsoft On the Issues
summary: Microsoft is implementing four new workforce initiatives to enhance employee relationships and workplace culture. These changes include removing non-competition clauses for most U.S. employees, strengthening protections against disclosure of alleged misconduct, increasing pay transparency by publicly disclosing salary ranges, and conducting a civil rights audit of its workforce policies. These initiatives aim to empower employees, foster a safe environment for concerns, and reinforce the company's commitment to diversity and inclusion.

title: Oracle closes $28B buy of ‘huge growth engine’ Cerner
summary: Oracle has completed its $28.3 billion acquisition of electronic health record company Cerner, marking its largest acquisition to date and a significant move into the healthcare sector. The deal, an all-cash tender offer of $95 per share, aims to make Cerner an "anchor asset" for Oracle's expansion into healthcare, focusing on improved usability and voice-enabled interfaces for medical software. This acquisition is a substantial digital health deal, following other major acquisitions in the industry, and positions Cerner as a standalone business unit within Oracle.

title: Procter & Gamble’s CIO believes passion is contagious. His latest passion: digitally remaking the 185-year-old company
summary: Vittorio Cretella, CIO at Procter & Gamble, is leading a massive digital transformation of the 185-year-old company. P&G has partnered with Microsoft to leverage the Microsoft Cloud, aiming to accelerate its digital manufacturing platform and enrich the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT). This collaboration seeks to improve productivity, speed up product delivery, boost customer satisfaction, and reduce costs, while also enhancing environmental sustainability through optimized energy and water consumption.

title: A Full Return to the Office? Does ‘Never’ Work for You?
summary: This article discusses the ongoing struggle between employers pushing for a return to office and employees who prefer remote work. It highlights that many companies are finding it difficult to enforce full-time office work, with some executives adapting to "remote-first" models or adopting hybrid approaches, while others, like C3 AI's CEO Tom Siebel, strongly advocate for employees to be in the office, citing competitive advantages and improved collaboration. The piece also notes a decrease in executive optimism regarding full in-office returns compared to early 2021.

title: Playbook of the Week: Automate Your Response to Zero-Day Exploitation of Atlassian Confluence
summary: This article introduces a Cortex XSOAR playbook designed to automate the response to the critical CVE-2022-26134 zero-day vulnerability in Atlassian Confluence Server and Data Center. The playbook helps security teams reduce manual effort by automating incident data enrichment, threat hunting across SIEMs and Palo Alto Networks environments, and remediation actions like blocking indicators and deploying detection rules. It is part of the Rapid Breach Response Pack, aiming to speed up the patching process and orchestration of security responses.

title: HYCU funding to aid multi-cloud data protection, management
summary: HYCU Inc. secured a $53 million Series B funding round, bringing its total funding to over $140 million. This investment will enable the company to expand its multi-cloud backup and recovery product line, increase its workforce, and develop a new data protection platform. HYCU aims to grow its customer base significantly and continues to pursue plans for an initial public offering, positioning itself as "recession-proof" in the data protection market.

title: 10 jobs with the best future outlook for college grads—some pay more than $100,000 per year
summary: The job market for 2022 college graduates is exceptionally strong, with nearly two job openings per unemployed person. ZipRecruiter identified 10 jobs with excellent future outlooks that require a bachelor's degree, based on Bureau of Labor Statistics projections. These roles, which include everything from elementary school teacher to financial manager, are expected to add tens to hundreds of thousands of new positions through 2030, with some paying over $100,000 annually.

title: Dow dives 800 points, S&P 500 posts worst week since January after inflation hits 40-year high
summary: U.S. stocks fell sharply on Friday, with the Dow dropping 880 points and the S&P 500 completing its worst week since January, following a higher-than-expected inflation report for May. The consumer price index reached its highest level since 1981, showing an 8.6% year-over-year increase, fueling concerns about a potential recession and prompting fears of a more aggressive Federal Reserve. Tech stocks, banks, and cyclical stocks were particularly impacted as the 2-year Treasury yield surged above 3%.

title: P&G Levels Up Manufacturing With Machine Learning and AI
summary: Procter & Gamble is partnering with Microsoft to implement AI, machine learning, and edge computing across over 100 manufacturing sites globally to improve productivity, reduce costs, and increase consumer satisfaction. This multiyear relationship will leverage Microsoft Azure to digitize and integrate data, enabling real-time, data-informed decisions and innovations in areas such as energy use, downtime reduction, and product quality. The collaboration includes the creation of a Digital Enablement Office to incubate and deploy high-priority business scenarios.

title: 3 Excellent Dividend-Stock ETFs
summary: This article highlights three excellent dividend-stock ETFs: Vanguard Dividend Appreciation ETF (VIG), Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF (SCHD), and Vanguard International High Dividend Yield Index ETF (VYMI). These ETFs are lauded for their low cost, sensible index construction, and backing by investor-friendly firms, catering to different dividend investment strategies. The author provides details on each ETF's methodology, performance, and the types of companies it invests in.

title: Hack Into Quantum Computing Boom With QQQ
summary: Quantum computing, a disruptive technology with significant growth potential, is still in its early stages but offers various use cases. While some speculative companies exist, major players in this field are large-cap companies. The Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) and Invesco NASDAQ 100 ETF (QQQM) provide investors with exposure to quantum computing through their holdings in established tech giants like Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet, Nvidia, and Honeywell.

title: Is the Roundhill Ball Metaverse ETF (METV) Right for You?
summary: The Roundhill Ball Metaverse ETF (METV) offers investors diversified exposure to companies benefiting from the metaverse's growth. This article examines METV's top holdings, including Meta Platforms, Nvidia, Roblox, Microsoft, and Autodesk, highlighting their roles in the metaverse ecosystem. It also discusses the fund's expense ratio and the potential market size of the metaverse industry.

title: Google Agrees to Pay $118 Million to Settle Pay Discrimination Case (Published 2022)
summary: Google has agreed to pay $118 million to settle a class-action lawsuit alleging systematic underpayment of women. The settlement covers approximately 15,500 women employed by Google in California since September 2013 and also mandates external oversight of its pay practices. Google denied wrongdoing, stating the settlement was in the best interest of all parties involved after five years of litigation.

title: Google Engineer Claims AI System is Sentient; China's Tech Giants Flourish as Crackdown Eases
summary: A Google engineer has been suspended after claiming that the company's LaMDA chatbot system shows signs of sentience, which Google denies, citing confidentiality breaches. Meanwhile, China's major tech companies like Baidu, Tencent, and Alibaba are experiencing a surge in share value as Beijing eases its regulatory crackdown on the sector. Twitter has also introduced a new "people-first" content moderation process to improve reporting of offensive content, especially amid Elon Musk's previous concerns about fake accounts.

title: Oracle women stumble in pay bias suit while Google cuts a deal
summary: Women at Oracle Corp. face a setback in their pay disparity lawsuit as a judge tentatively revoked their class-action status, making it more difficult to proceed. Meanwhile, Google agreed to pay $118 million to settle a similar lawsuit alleging pay disparities for more than 15,000 female workers. The Google settlement includes provisions for independent oversight of hiring practices and pay equity studies.

title: Next-Generation Adobe Analytics Delivers Customer Insights From Streaming Media and the Metaverse
summary: Adobe has launched new services for Adobe Analytics, creating a unified workspace for brands to gather data and insights from various media, including the metaverse and streaming content. This update allows for seamless data migration from other analytics platforms, ensuring compliance with regulations like GDPR and CCPA. By supporting emerging channels, Adobe Analytics aims to provide comprehensive omnichannel analysis through Customer Journey Analytics, helping businesses understand evolving consumer behaviors and deliver personalized experiences.

title: The CISOs Report: A spotlight on today’s cybersecurity challenges
summary: A new report, in partnership with Zscaler and the Cloud Security Alliance, surveyed over 400 CISOs globally to identify their primary cybersecurity challenges. The findings indicate that 80% of C-level executives prioritize zero trust, with most organizations experiencing material damage from cyber attacks in the past year. The article highlights key threats like ransomware and supply-chain attacks, stresses the importance of securing third-party risks, and offers recommendations such as network-agnostic architecture and immediate zero trust implementation.

title: How Jabil’s New HQ Facilitates Collaboration Between Worldwide Teams
summary: Jabil, a global technology solutions company with 260,000 employees worldwide, opened a new 175,000-square-foot headquarters in St. Petersburg, Florida, designed to foster collaboration. The facility, equipped with state-of-the-art Crestron technology, allows seamless communication between local and international teams. Clearwater, Fla.-based APG Technology was the audiovisual integrator for the project, ensuring a uniform and user-friendly experience across various collaboration spaces.

title: P&G taps Microsoft for cloud services to boost production efficiency
summary: Procter & Gamble has partnered with Microsoft to utilize its Azure cloud computing services and predictive analytics to enhance manufacturing efficiency, reduce costs, and improve product delivery. This collaboration aims to leverage digital manufacturing visibility and advanced analytics to optimize production processes for various P&G products globally. The initiative builds on four years of prior cooperation, focusing on better data utilization, automation, digital twins, and sustainability.

title: National Grid's CIDO reimagines operating models, IT strategy
summary: Adriana Karaboutis, National Grid's group chief information and digital officer (CIDO), discusses her approach to digitizing the company. She outlines a strategy that balances legacy IT with emerging technologies like AI, machine learning, and cloud computing, emphasizing a product operating model and agile methodologies. Karaboutis also highlights the CIDO's role in measuring and supporting sustainability initiatives and navigating the challenges of existing legacy infrastructure.

title: L3Harris in talks to buy Israeli spyware firm NSO - reports
summary: U.S. defence contractor L3Harris is reportedly in talks to acquire Israeli spyware firm NSO Group, a deal that would require approvals from U.S. and Israeli authorities and L3Harris's board. The potential acquisition raises concerns in the White House due to NSO's controversial Pegasus software, which has been used by governments to spy on individuals, leading to the company being blacklisted by the U.S. Commerce Department. If approved, the deal could potentially remove NSO from the banned list and allow its assets to be exclusively used with the United States and its allies.

title: Procter & Gamble Partners With Microsoft To Transform And Accelerate Digital Manufacturing
summary: Procter & Gamble (P&G) has partnered with Microsoft to advance digital manufacturing through cloud, AI, and digital transformation technologies. This multiyear collaboration aims to make manufacturing smarter by utilizing Microsoft Cloud, Azure data, and AI solutions to optimize P&G's manufacturing and packaging processes, initially focusing on diaper and paper towel production. The initiative seeks to improve predictive quality, reduce downtime, enhance supply chain efficiency, and explore the concept of an "industrial metaverse" for simulating manufacturing environments.

title: Leidos Announces 2022 Supplier Innovation & Technology Award Winners
summary: Leidos announced the recipients of its 2022 Supplier Innovation & Technology awards, recognizing partners for excellence in technology, collaboration, partnership, and innovation. The awards, presented at a symposium, included new categories like Secure Supply Chain Supplier of the Year. Cisco, ServiceNow, Carahsoft, Thundercat Technologies LLC, CyberCore Technologies, and HashiCorp were among the winners in various categories.

title: Microsoft Targets Salesforce Clients With New Tools to Aid Sales Reps
summary: Microsoft has introduced Viva Sales, a new program designed to integrate its Office and Teams applications with customer-relationship management (CRM) software, including its own and rival platforms like Salesforce. This initiative aims to attract Salesforce clients by allowing data synchronization between CRM systems and Microsoft's productivity suite. Viva Sales also incorporates AI tools to analyze sales calls, track customer sentiment, and provide actionable feedback to sales representatives.

title: Ahead of the Game: D-Wave Delivers Prototype of Next-Generation Advantage2 Annealing Quantum Computer
summary: D-Wave has announced the release of an experimental prototype for its next-generation Advantage2 annealing quantum computer, available through its Leap quantum cloud service. This prototype features over 500 qubits with a new Zephyr topology and 20-way inter-qubit connectivity, demonstrating early performance gains such as reduced error rates and improved solution quality. The full Advantage2 system, expected in 2023-2024, will boast 7,000 qubits and an innovative low-noise fabrication process, building on D-Wave's 15 years of experience in quantum annealing technology.

title: Salesforce Sales Cloud Unlimited Edition adds AI, automation
summary: Salesforce has integrated eight AI and automation tools into its Sales Cloud Unlimited Edition, maintaining the current pricing of $300 per user per month. This move aims to streamline operations and enhance sales productivity by automating manual tasks. Additionally, Salesforce plans to incorporate sales-oriented Slack features through its acquisition of Troops.ai, and Box Inc. has deepened its integration with Salesforce to include e-signature functionality and support for Salesforce Flow.

title: ServiceNow Inc. stock underperforms Thursday when compared to competitors
summary: ServiceNow Inc. (NOW) stock fell 8.13% on Thursday, closing at $428.08, significantly underperforming the broader market which also saw declines. This drop ended a two-day winning streak for the company. ServiceNow's stock also underperformed compared to competitors like Microsoft, Qualcomm, and IBM, and closed $279.52 below its 52-week high.

title: Broadcom's acquire-and-axe history concerns VMware users
summary: VMware users and employees are expressing concern over Broadcom's acquisition of the company, fearing a repeat of Broadcom's historical strategy of acquiring and then divesting parts of companies. Broadcom's CEO, Hock Tan, intends to transition VMware to a subscription-based model and integrate Broadcom's infrastructure and security software. The acquisition timing also coincides with a trend where corporate IT shops are moving towards SaaS-based solutions, diminishing VMware's traditional market.

title: Is Juneteenth being observed by companies in the Dow industrials? Here's how some are handling it.
summary: This article explores how companies in the Dow industrials are observing Juneteenth, a federal holiday. While many Dow components are closed, some are open, and others offer employees the choice to take it as a paid holiday. The article also notes the relatively quick adoption of Juneteenth as a day off for exchanges compared to Martin Luther King, Jr. Day.

title: Native Advertising Examples: 17 of the Best and Most Inspiring Native Ads
summary: This article showcases 17 successful native advertising campaigns by various global brands, highlighting how native ads integrate seamlessly into content to drive engagement, awareness, and sales. It emphasizes native advertising's effectiveness as a non-interruptive and contextually relevant alternative to traditional ads, detailing increased CTRs, lead generation, and ROAS achieved by companies like Adidas, Vodafone, and Square Yards through platforms like Taboola. The article concludes by reinforcing why native advertising is a powerful digital marketing technique, citing its non-disruptive nature and contextual relevance.

title: Why ESG is Becoming a Bigger Deal for Investors
summary: ESG (environmental, social, and governance) investing is rapidly gaining traction, with a record $649 billion poured into ESG-focused funds in 2021. Major players like BlackRock are emphasizing ESG, believing that companies deliberating on their societal role perform better, leading to long-term value for shareholders. While greenwashing concerns exist, new global standards and regulatory clarifications are emerging as ESG becomes a mainstream method for evaluating businesses and attracting investment.

title: The Hong Kong Management Association and Microsoft Hong Kong Showcase Technology Excellence, Innovation and Resilience – Microsoft News Center Hong Kong
summary: The Hong Kong Management Association (HKMA) and Microsoft Hong Kong (MSHK) recognized 14 Hong Kong companies for their innovative use of technology in the inaugural HKMA x MSHK Excellence in Digital Transformation. These companies demonstrated successful integration of various technologies, including cloud, big data, and AI, across five categories: customer engagement, employee empowerment, product transformation, operations optimization, and all-rounded innovation. The initiative highlights Hong Kong businesses' agility in leveraging technology to navigate challenges, seize opportunities, and enhance operational models.

title: A closer look at P&G’s ‘water positive’ pledge
summary: Procter & Gamble has announced a "water positive" goal by 2030, aiming to restore more water than its operations and products consume. The initiative includes two new restoration pledges focusing on water consumed during manufacturing and by household product use in 18 water-stressed regions, primarily Los Angeles and Mexico City. P&G is investing in various restoration projects and integrating sustainability metrics into executive compensation, while experts commend the company's rigorous approach to consumer-use impact but call for more engagement with public policy for broader impact.

title: Corsair Dark Core RGB Pro SE wireless gaming mouse review
summary: The Corsair Dark Core RGB Pro SE is a heavy, feature-rich wireless gaming mouse offering excellent connectivity and ergonomics. While praised for its build quality, customizable RGB, and precise sensor, its significant weight (142g) and mediocre battery life (20 hours with RGB on) are notable drawbacks, especially for competitive FPS players. The review concludes that it's a great option for those who prefer comfortable, heavier mice for productivity and slower-paced games, rather than twitch shooters.

title: Microsoft Office 365 has ability to ‘spy’ on workers
summary: Research has revealed that Microsoft Office 365 contains tools that allow employers to monitor staff emails and computer usage, raising privacy concerns. Despite Microsoft's 2020 changes to protect employee privacy by aggregating data, UCL research found that "content search" and "audit" tools still enable detailed individual surveillance. This has led to calls for Microsoft to increase transparency and notify employees when such monitoring tools are enabled.

title: First Watch Adds Bumble Executive Stephanie Lilak to Board of Directors
summary: First Watch Restaurant Group has appointed Stephanie Lilak, Chief People Officer of Bumble Inc., to its Board of Directors, effective June 17, 2022. Lilak will join the Audit Committee and Compensation Committee, bringing extensive human resources experience from her roles at Bumble Inc., Dunkin’ Brands, and General Mills. Her appointment is expected to support First Watch’s growth and its people-centric "You First" culture.

title: Oracle introduces lower-cost version of its full on-premises cloud stack
summary: Oracle has introduced a more affordable version of its on-premises cloud stack, Dedicated Region Cloud@Customer, alongside a new rack-level offering called Oracle Compute Cloud@Customer. The new Dedicated Region Cloud@Customer reduces the required space and annual cost significantly, making Oracle's full public cloud services, including Fusion applications, accessible to a broader range of global companies for workloads that cannot fully migrate to the public cloud. Oracle Compute Cloud@Customer provides managed on-site computing and storage resources for smaller workloads, similar to offerings from AWS, Microsoft, and Google.

title: YPF explora la Computación Cuántica para el desarrollo de la transición energética junto a Microsoft
summary: YPF is partnering with Microsoft to explore the use of quantum computing for developing energy transition sources and retraining its technical teams. The project aims to accelerate the adoption of renewable energy and reinforce YPF's commitment to sustainability. It began with a training program for YPF's Digital Technologies teams, led by Microsoft experts, to identify potential pilot applications in 2022.

title: Microsoft stops selling emotion-reading tech, limits face recognition
summary: Microsoft Corp announced it will stop selling emotion-reading technology based on facial images and will also limit unfettered access to its facial recognition technology. This move aligns with efforts by leading cloud providers to self-regulate sensitive technologies as lawmakers consider new legal limits. Existing customers of emotion-reading tools will have one year before losing access, and facial recognition services will now require approval for use.

title: Tech companies still scooping up office space and Vancouver’s feeling the squeeze
summary: Despite the rise of remote work, Vancouver's downtown office vacancy rate remains low at 7.4%, driven by demand from large tech companies. These companies are drawn to Vancouver due to lower operating costs compared to other major tech hubs. However, this demand is making office space expensive, with Vancouver having the highest per-square-foot cost in Canada.

title: MinIO extends Snowflake analysis to any data location
summary: MinIO has partnered with Snowflake to enable Snowflake analytics on data stored in any location, not just within Snowflake's own environment. This partnership allows customers to leverage external table support in MinIO for cost-effective analysis of large datasets without moving them to the cloud. This provides flexibility similar to recent Snowflake partnerships with Dell and Pure Storage, offering various options for on-premises or cloud-based data analysis.

title: Avnet, and Amazon Web Services enters into a global strategic partnership
summary: Avnet and Amazon Web Services (AWS) have formed a global strategic partnership aimed at helping Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs) of IoT solutions accelerate their time to market. This collaboration will enable Avnet’s IoTConnect Platform to leverage AWS's extensive portfolio of services, creating a scalable and secure platform for application-specific usage. The partnership provides OEMs with pre-integrated and abstracted capabilities, such as device provisioning, multi-layer security, and business intelligence, allowing them to focus on differentiating their connected products.

title: Cloudflare recognized by Microsoft as a Security Software Innovator
summary: Cloudflare announced it has won the Security Software Innovator award at the 2022 Microsoft Security Excellence Awards. This recognition highlights Cloudflare's innovative approach to Zero Trust and security solutions through deep integrations with Microsoft, helping joint customers secure their web applications and employees. The article emphasizes the importance of Zero Trust in the modern threat landscape, detailing Cloudflare One's comprehensive capabilities.

title: Microsoft Viva Sales takes on Salesforce-Slack tandem
summary: Microsoft is set to launch Viva Sales, an AI-powered automation tool designed to integrate sales data from Microsoft 365 and Teams directly into CRM systems, challenging Salesforce's offerings. Viva Sales aims to streamline sales processes by reducing manual data entry and app-switching, particularly for remote workers. This move intensifies the rivalry between Microsoft and Salesforce, with both companies focusing on enhancing employee experience through AI and automation in sales.

title: ECOLAB3D™: Putting Real Time Data to Work for Industrial Water Management
summary: ECOLAB3D is an IIOT platform built on Microsoft Azure that uses real-time data, AI, and machine learning to optimize industrial water management. It helps companies achieve performance, compliance, and savings goals by providing actionable insights from diverse system data. The platform has achieved SOC 2 Type I certification, demonstrating its commitment to data security and integrity for customers.

title: BWT Alpine F1 Team turns big data into faster track times with data science platform built on Azure and Azure NetApp Files
summary: BWT Alpine F1 Team implemented a new cloud-hosted data science platform using Microsoft Azure and Azure NetApp Files to enhance race performance. The platform integrates racing, testing, and manufacturing data, emphasizing "fast data" to enable quick decision-making for engineers. This move has allowed Alpine to rapidly scale resources, manage costs effectively, and improve productivity.

title: NYLI Winslow Focused Large Cap Growth ETF ETF Price, Holdings, & News (NYSEARCA:IWFG)
summary: The NYLI Winslow Focused Large Cap Growth ETF (IWFG) is an actively managed, non-transparent ETF focused on achieving long-term capital appreciation by investing in US large-cap growth companies. Launched on June 23, 2022, and managed by IndexIQ, the ETF had assets under management of $60.06 million as of July 2, 2026, with a net expense ratio of 0.65%. Its top holdings include major tech companies like NVIDIA, Microsoft, Apple, and Alphabet.

title: Roe v. Wade overturned: Here are companies paying for abortion travel costs for employees
summary: Following the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade, numerous major U.S. companies announced expanded support and financial assistance for employees seeking abortions in states with new restrictions. This support often includes covering travel expenses for medical care unavailable in their home states. Corporations are responding to pressure from investors, customers, and employees, and are concerned about the impact on talent attraction and retention.

title: Disney, other U.S. companies offer abortion travel benefit after Roe decision
summary: Following the U.S. Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade, numerous U.S. companies, including Walt Disney Co. and Meta Platforms Inc., announced they would cover travel expenses for employees seeking abortion services. This move comes as many states are expected to restrict or ban abortions, making it necessary for employees to travel to states where the procedure remains legal. Companies like Dick's Sporting Goods, Lyft, Yelp, Microsoft, Tesla, Apple, Alaska Air Group, Johnson & Johnson, OkCupid, Bumble, Netflix, and JPMorgan Chase & Co. are also offering similar benefits or legal protections.

title: Five9 Integration with Microsoft Teams Review
summary: This article reviews the integration of Five9 with Microsoft Teams, highlighting how it enhances customer service by connecting agents with subject matter experts in real-time. The integration offers features like agent-expert consultation and telephony connect, aiming to bridge communication gaps and improve customer experience. It details benefits such as full organizational collaboration, boosted CX, simplified directories, toll-free call transfers, and an improved employee experience.

title: IICS 2022: How to Secure Essential Infrastructure Systems Against Cyber Threats
summary: The article discusses the critical need to secure essential infrastructure systems against cyber threats, emphasizing that these attacks are borderless and require global collaboration between public and private sectors. Cybersecurity experts gathered at IICS 2022 highlighted the urgency of addressing both information technology (IT) and operational technology (OT) vulnerabilities, advocating for greater consistency in requirements and collaboration among governments and vendors. They stressed that IT and OT must integrate their efforts to achieve true security from cyberattacks.

title: Ransomware rising: A look at ThreatLabz’ latest findings
summary: A report from Zscaler's ThreatLabz indicates a significant increase in ransomware attacks, with an 80% rise between February 2021 and March 2022, and a 120% jump in double extortion incidents. Manufacturing remains the most targeted industry, while the use of ransomware-as-a-service (RaaS) and supply chain attacks are also increasing. The article emphasizes that zero trust principles and employee education are crucial defenses against these evolving threats.

title: Abortion assistance: Kroger to offer up to $4,000 of out-of-state travel costs for employees seeking abortion
summary: Kroger announced it will offer up to $4,000 to cover out-of-state travel costs for employees seeking abortion and fertility treatments, following the Supreme Court's decision to overturn Roe v. Wade. The company, headquartered in Cincinnati, operates stores in states like Ohio and Kentucky where abortion is now banned or mostly banned. This move aligns Kroger with nearly two dozen other major U.S. companies providing similar assistance.

title: HoloLens 2 helps Novo Nordisk employees see work in new ways
summary: Novo Nordisk is implementing Microsoft HoloLens 2 and related Dynamics 365 technologies to transform its manufacturing operations and employee training. This includes using augmented instructions for complex procedures and facilitating virtual site visits, significantly improving efficiency, onboarding, and reducing travel needs across its global facilities. The technology has been well-received by employees, leading to improved performance consistency and a more flexible workplace.

title: KPMG leads Digital Future of Work hackathon
summary: KPMG, in collaboration with Microsoft, BP plc, and the University of Cambridge Think Lab, hosted a two-day "Digital Future of Work" hackathon in London. The event focused on developing digital solutions for modern business challenges, including talent retention and hybrid work, aligning with the UN's Sustainable Development Goal of "Decent work and economic growth." The winning solution, "The Good Job Tool," helps design roles that meet candidate expectations and market demands, receiving investment and support from KPMG.

title: Why treasury automation is a must
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic significantly accelerated the urgency of treasury automation for corporate treasurers. Companies had to quickly adopt digital processes to ensure resilience and maintain cash visibility amidst lockdowns and supply chain disruptions. The article highlights that automation is an ongoing task, with banks and fintechs collaborating to provide accessible and cost-effective solutions for tasks like cash flow forecasting, receivables reconciliation, and liquidity management, which were previously out of reach for many businesses.

title: Best Digital Planner for OneNote
summary: The article identifies the Key2Success OneNote Digital Planner as the top choice for 2024, highlighting its professional design and goal-oriented system. It outlines various editions available (Personal, Professional, Business, Executive) and new features like customizable pages and team tools in the Business Executive version. The planner is praised for syncing across multiple devices and its continuous improvement based on user feedback.

title: HDFC Bank-backed Lentra AI to acquire TheDataTeam
summary: Digital lending platform Lentra AI, backed by HDFC Bank, has acquired artificial intelligence solutions company TheDataTeam for an undisclosed amount. The acquisition aims to enhance Lentra's offerings by integrating TheDataTeam's Cadenz behavior intelligence platform to help banks and financial institutions make better data-driven decisions on customer loan repayment histories. Rangarajan Vasudevan, founder of TheDataTeam, will join Lentra as co-founder and chief data officer, strengthening Lentra's position in the credit market.

title: FabricScape: Escaping Service Fabric and Taking Over the Cluster
summary: Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 researchers identified FabricScape (CVE-2022-30137), an important vulnerability in Microsoft's Service Fabric that allows Linux containers to escalate privileges and gain root access, potentially compromising an entire cluster. This vulnerability affects Azure Service Fabric and other Microsoft products using it, though certain managed multi-tenant services have runtime access disabled, preventing exploitation. Microsoft has patched the issue, and users not on automatic updates are advised to upgrade their Linux clusters.

title: Accenture and Avanade Named Microsoft 2022 Global SI Partner of the Year for 17th Time
summary: Accenture and Avanade have been named the Microsoft 2022 Global SI Partner of the Year for the 17th time, a record achievement. They also received ten additional awards, including several country-level Partner of the Year awards, recognizing their excellence in innovation and implementation of customer solutions based on Microsoft technology. This acknowledges their combined service capabilities, global scale, and solution development in solving complex client challenges and addressing sustainability.

title: I tried Elon Musk's Starlink internet on a Royal Caribbean cruise ship
summary: The author tested Elon Musk's Starlink internet on Royal Caribbean's Freedom of the Seas. Initial speeds were significantly faster than Royal Caribbean's typical Voom service, allowing for streaming and Zoom calls. While speeds varied slightly in different ship locations, Starlink generally far exceeded expectations for internet at sea.

title: News | KKR in Talks To Buy Microsoft-Occupied Office Buildings in Atlanta
summary: Private equity firm KKR is in discussions to acquire two office buildings in Atlanta, totaling 523,000 square feet, which are fully occupied by Microsoft. The buildings, located at Atlantic Yards, were developed by Invesco and Hines. This potential acquisition highlights significant investment activity in prime office real estate.

title: |‘Sokaiya’ gone, but scandals continue at listed companies
summary: |Corporate racketeering, once a significant problem in Japan with "sokaiya" disrupting shareholder meetings, has drastically declined due to revised laws and police crackdowns. However, despite the decline in racketeering, major Japanese companies like Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group and Mitsubishi Electric Corp. faced new types of scandals prompting apologies at their annual shareholder meetings. These incidents highlight ongoing corporate governance issues, including market manipulation and product quality control misconduct, leading to pledges for improved internal measures and transparency.

title: DISA looks to install 10GB ethernet line from Equinix data center to DHS facility
summary: The Defense Information Systems Agency (DISA) is seeking bids to install and maintain a 10GB ethernet line connecting an Equinix data center in Dallas, Texas, to a Department of Homeland Security (DHS) facility in Pensacola, Florida. This initiative supports DHS's ongoing cloud migration efforts, which involve shifting workloads from their current data centers to cloud providers like AWS. The move comes amid continued spending on existing facilities and some controversy surrounding cloud contracts with human rights groups and Google employees protesting deals with ICE.

title: Announcing the 2022 Microsoft US Award Winners
summary: Microsoft has announced the winners of its 2022 US Partner Awards, which complement the global Microsoft Partner of the Year program by highlighting US-specific partner impact. The awards recognize partners across various categories including Azure AI, Business Applications, Business Excellence, Modern Work & Security, Social Impact, and Industry-specific solutions. The announcement encourages partners to register for the upcoming Microsoft Inspire virtual event on July 19-20, 2022.

title: Sharebite Raises Additional $39M in Series B
summary: Sharebite, a corporate food ordering platform, has raised an additional $39 million in a Series B funding round, led by Prosus, one of the world's largest technology investors. The company, which saw a 30x increase in daily order volume in 2021, plans to use the investment to expand its footprint and launch new products for modern workplaces. This funding follows a partnership with Vornado Realty Trust, making Sharebite the exclusive office meal solution in 20.6 million square feet of Manhattan office space.

title: Watch: When Microsoft CEO Steve Ballmer laughed at iPhone
summary: This article revisits a famous incident where then-Microsoft CEO Steve Ballmer publicly dismissed the original Apple iPhone upon its launch. He criticized its high price and lack of a physical keyboard, believing it wouldn't appeal to business users. Years later, Ballmer admitted his mistake, acknowledging Apple's innovative business model and regretting Microsoft's slow entry into the hardware business for mobile devices.

title: HPE Is The First Big OEM To Adopt Ampere Computing Arm Chips
summary: HPE has announced its adoption of Ampere Computing's "Mystique" Altra Max Arm server chip in its standard ProLiant rack-mounted server, marking Ampere's first major OEM server maker partnership. This move, showcased with the ProLiant RL300 server, signifies HPE's renewed commitment to Arm-based processors after previous cautious ventures. The decision is driven by the Altra chips' deterministic performance and competitive price/performance, particularly for cloud-native workloads, positioning HPE to compete aggressively against Intel Xeon and AMD Epyc processors.

title: Merck and NJIT's New Jersey Innovation Institute Partner on Health Care Startup Development
summary: Merck and the New Jersey Innovation Institute (NJII) have launched the Merck Digital Sciences Studio (MDSS) to foster innovative technologies for drug discovery and development. The MDSS will support early-stage biomedical startups, particularly those focusing on AI and machine learning, with direct investment, cloud computing access, and opportunities to pilot technologies with Merck scientists. This collaboration aims to accelerate digital technologies in pharmaceutical research and development through locations in Newark, N.J., and Cambridge, Mass.

title: Discord IPO: Everything to know about Discord
summary: This article provides an in-depth look at Discord ahead of its anticipated IPO, covering its valuation, business model, competitors, and growth strategy. It details how the company generates revenue primarily through its Nitro subscription service and outlines its efforts to expand beyond its core gaming audience. The piece also discusses Discord's profitability status, ownership, and key personnel.

title: BP, Shell To Pay Employee Travel Costs After Abortion Ruling
summary: Following the U.S. Supreme Court's reversal of Roe v. Wade, BP Plc and Shell Plc announced they would cover travel expenses for U.S. employees needing to access health services not available near their homes. This makes them the first major oil companies to implement such policies. Both companies maintain significant operations in Texas, a state expected to ban or severely restrict abortions, joining other corporate giants in expanding employee health benefits.

title: Corsair TC200 gaming chair review: "A great chair for both work and play"
summary: The Corsair TC200 gaming chair offers significant improvements over its predecessor, the T3 Rush, particularly for larger users with its wider seat and back, and internal lumbar support. Reviewer Frederick Hillinger praises its all-day comfort for both work and gaming, despite the lumbar support not being adjustable. The chair is highly recommended for its strong value, high-quality materials, and thoughtful design that incorporates user feedback.

title: DevOps 2030: People, Practices, And Platforms
summary: DevOps has proven its value in software-intensive organizations by reducing time-to-market, increasing agility, and enhancing resilience. Looking ahead to 2030, the evolution of DevOps will focus on three key areas: people, practices, and platforms. Success will involve fine-tuning team integration, automating processes to free up human attention, and consolidating and expanding DevOps platforms to support new technologies like low/no-code apps and MLOps.

title: Cloudera embraces Apache Iceberg as cloud data lake evolves
summary: Cloudera has announced support for Apache Iceberg, an open-source cloud data lake table format, within its Cloudera Data Platform. This move signifies Cloudera's continued evolution from its Hadoop roots towards modern cloud data lake technology. The company believes Iceberg enhances its ability to work with various cloud providers and analytical engines, addressing the growing need for flexible and structured data lake solutions in enterprise environments.

title: Will Zoom Stock Hit $1,500 a Share by 2026?
summary: This article examines Ark Invest's bold prediction that Zoom (ZM) stock could reach $1,500 per share by 2026. While Ark Invest's model, driven by factors like increased remote work, expanding unified communications market share, and revenue growth from new AI-driven products, suggests this possibility, the article highlights the significant discrepancy between Ark's projected 76% annual growth and Zoom's actual present growth rate of around 10-12%. Nanalyze questions the sustainability of such aggressive growth projections and advises caution for investors.

title: Up in the Cloud!
summary: This article by Uma Iyer discusses the evolving concept of cloud computing, moving beyond its abstract perception to its tangible impact on technology and data management. It explores the differences between cloud storage and cloud computing, highlights real-world applications and the benefits of scalability and ease of use, and addresses the critical issue of trust and security in cloud technologies through various models and programs like CSA STAR. The article concludes by looking at emerging trends like edge computing, indicating a bright future for cloud technology.
